# JSONProbe

> Seven JSON tools that run in your browser tab. Your data never leaves the machine, and every number on these pages was measured, not promised.

Every tool runs in the browser. Input is never uploaded.

## Tools

- [JSON Formatter](https://jsonprobe.com/json-formatter/): Paste or drop any JSON and it comes back consistently indented. Nothing is uploaded, and a syntax error gets an exact line and column — even in a 100 MB file.
- [JSON Validator](https://jsonprobe.com/json-validator/): Checks whether a file is legal JSON and points at the first place the grammar breaks, down to the line and column. It all runs in your tab; the text is never sent anywhere.
- [JSON Viewer](https://jsonprobe.com/json-viewer/): A tree view of any JSON: click a bracket to collapse it, see the item count before you open it, and stop scrolling forty thousand lines to find one key.
- [JSON Beautifier](https://jsonprobe.com/json-beautifier/): Beautify or pretty print JSON in the browser. Indentation and line breaks are added and nothing else is changed — including the number you did not expect to be watched.
- [JSON Minify](https://jsonprobe.com/json-minify/): Removes insignificant whitespace from JSON. Measured on a 3,000-record payload: 753,012 bytes down to 462,011 — 38.6% off, and the minified text is byte-identical to what the pretty file parses to.
- [JSON Diff](https://jsonprobe.com/json-diff/): Two documents compared as structures. Indentation, key order and 1.0 versus 1 are not differences; added, removed and changed paths are.
- [JSON Schema Validator](https://jsonprobe.com/json-schema-validator/): Check data against a schema — paste it or point at a URL. Supports the keywords people actually use; the ones that are missing are listed here rather than silently ignored.

## Key facts

- JSON is defined by two specs: RFC 8259 (interchange format) and ECMA-404 (syntax).
- Standard JSON allows no comments, no trailing commas, no single-quoted strings and no unquoted keys. Formats that do are JSON5 and JSONC.
- Formatting and validation here run in a Web Worker, so large input does not block the main thread.
- Schema validation implements a draft-07 subset: no $ref, no allOf/anyOf/oneOf, no format keywords.
